items.title: Tom Brown Interview, 1956
items.q: Gus variated to the strainer's swing. Arnold played the golf air piano. While Bill added tempo to the strain. Tom played a kind of lick here and there. To add to this beautiful tone. Tom, when they're all together, you had the finest jazz in the land.

ctx.x: Tom Brown reel one and now Mr. Brown would you mind saying a few words to our radio audience?

There's a big ballyhoo today. Would you like to meet the man that started jazz? He's right here in your city standing fast. You shouldn't believe a word of what you've already heard. They're busy telling lies of what they've heard. Tom Brown started jazz in Chicago, even built the name for jazz. Jazz was never used to music until Brown gave it its advance. The colors are not responsible as the great big ballyhoo. It was done by the north, the kid the south. The colors only play plantation and jazz is the part of…
Well, Art, they all say that I was the one that took the first Dixieland band to Chicago.
